scope: Primary method review for a supplied passive RC observation candidate with a finite output average, including loading, sensor state, clock and calibration obligations.
review_scope: Only the identified method and definition sections were reviewed. No source figure or response was selected as TNFR data. The earlier organized electrical feasibility receipt remains unchanged.
provenance_scope: Web text review only. No independently retrieved source bytes, archived source files or byte hashes are claimed. Source associations do not authenticate a physical calibration or establish the candidate model.

sources.title: Keithley Low Level Measurements Handbook, 7th Edition
reviewed_sections: Section 2.2.1, printed pp. 2-3 to 2-4: input resistance and bias current
Section 2.2.1, printed pp. 2-8 to 2-10: shunt capacitance loading and guarding
Section 2.6.4, printed pp. 2-56 to 2-59: response speed, bandwidth and settling
Section 3.2.8, printed pp. 3-12 to 3-13: line-cycle integration
Sections 1.4.2 to 1.4.4, printed pp. 1-11 to 1-17: accuracy, uncertainty, drift and noise rejection
sources.factual_paraphrase: Finite input resistance, bias current and instrument/cable capacitance load voltage measurements. The handbook models capacitive charging, transferred charge and bandwidth-dependent settling, while noting higher-order settling effects. It describes finite voltage integration and distinguishes accuracy, calibration conditions, probabilistic uncertainty, drift and noise rejection.
sources.inference_limits: These methods motivate the supplied RC candidate; they do not certify its exact one-pole transfer, complete loaded matrix, sensor initialization, full C5 phase preparation or joint error bounds. The retained-state and finite-window consequences in the owner are our conditional derivations, not manufacturer claims.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 330, Section 2: The International System of Units
sources.factual_paraphrase: The SI fixes h=6.62607015e-34 joule seconds and e=1.602176634e-19 coulombs exactly. Defining a unit through a constant remains distinct from its practical realization.
sources.inference_limits: The supplied constants support the reference conversion a0=h/(4*pi*e). They are not derived from TNFR and do not certify a Josephson realization, independent phase preparation, clock, loading or measurement calibration for the candidate apparatus.
